text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- With the help of extensive marketing campaigns worth 40 million crowns Alm. Brand Bank grew from being number twelve on the list of Denmark's largest banks to being number nine in 1996. The bank's deposits rose by 29 percent to 5.5 billion crowns while loans rose by 22 percent to 3.1 billion crowns.

--- A group of Danish institutional investors has bought a majority stake in US biotechnology company Receptor Technologies Inc for 82 million crowns. The company has establised a subsidiary west of Copenhagen with 50 employees to handle research in medicine to fight among others HIV and neurological diseases.
--- In a new bill to be presented by tax minister Carsten Koch within a month, taxes on a number of company fringe benefits are to be lowered and taxes on company PCs at home are to be abolished.
--- Charter companies sell more than 10 percent of their aircraft space as "seat only" without hotel stays, forcing SAS to lower prices.

--- At least 60 Danish companies have set up production in China and more are on their way. Total Danish investments in China are worth three billion crowns at present, the largest total investment made by Danish companies on one market.
--- Telecom group Tele Danmark in cooperation with French telecom company Nethold and Norwegian telecom company Telenor is stands to win most of the future digital TV market in the nordic countries.
